instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about waist height and stand facing the anchor.
2. Grip the handles with palms facing down, hands wider than shoulder width.
3. Walk your feet forward and lean back with body straight, heels on the floor and arms extended.
4. Pull your chest toward the handles by driving your elbows out and back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the elbows wide and back to load the rhomboids and rear delts.
2. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
3. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.
4. Lower your feet to increase difficulty or step them back to make it easier.

instructions:
1. Stand side-on to the net in a balanced ready stance with knees slightly bent.
2. Rotate your hips and trunk back to load the racket on your dominant side.
3. Step forward and drive from the back leg, uncoiling your hips and trunk toward the ball.
4. Swing the racket forward, contacting the ball in front of your body with the wrist firm.
5. Follow through across your body and recover to the ready stance.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Generate power from the ground up: legs, then hips, then trunk, then arm.
2. Keep your eyes on the ball through contact.
3. Brace your core to transfer rotation into the stroke.
4. Finish the follow-through fully rather than cutting the swing short.

instructions:
1. Stand on the treadmill side rails and attach the safety clip to your clothing.
2. Start the belt at a low speed and step on carefully.
3. Increase the speed to a comfortable jogging pace with an upright posture and braced core.
4. Bend your arms to about 90 degrees and swing them naturally at your sides.
5. Land mid-foot with each stride and keep your breathing steady.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your head up and gaze forward, not down at your feet.
2. Use a smooth, natural stride to reduce joint impact.
3. Set a pace that lets you hold good form for the full duration.
4. Drive your arms to help maintain rhythm.

instructions:
1. Stand on the treadmill side rails and attach the safety clip to your clothing.
2. Start the belt at a low speed and step on carefully.
3. Increase the speed to a comfortable walking pace with an upright posture.
4. Take natural strides, rolling from heel to toe with each step.
5. Swing your arms gently and keep your breathing relaxed.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your head up and shoulders relaxed.
2. Avoid holding the handrails so your core and posture stay engaged.
3. Add incline to increase glute, hamstring and calf demand.
4. Maintain a steady, comfortable pace throughout.
